question: I'm using Python. What does weave.init do, and what project string should I pass?
answer:
In Python, `weave.init()` sets up Weave tracing for a project. Pass a string in the form `"<your-team>/<your-project>"`: your CoreWeave Forge team name and your Weights & Biases project name [S2].

**What it does**
- It registers your team and project with Weave. The SDK uses this to send spans to the right place in the UI [S4].
- In the agent-tracing quickstart, it authenticates with Weights & Biases and configures the OpenTelemetry (OTel) exporter that sends agent spans to the **Agents** view [S1].
- If the project doesn't exist on your team yet, Weave creates it the first time you write to it [S1].
- It returns a client. The getting-started example assigns it with `client = weave.init(...)` [S2].
- For agent tracing, call it before `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()`, `start_llm()`, `start_tool()` or `start_subagent()`. Those functions silently do nothing if the init call is absent [S4].

**What to pass**
```python
import weave

client = weave.init("my-team/my-project")  # replace with your team and project
```
- The `team/project` form is what the Python docs show [S2][S4].
- An integration page also says you can pass just a project name, such as `"verdict_demo"`, to log to your default team or entity [S3]. That page documents this for the Verdict integration, so I'm treating it as general behavior of `weave.init`. I didn't find a Python SDK reference page for `init` that confirms it.
- Use the full `team/project` string if you want to be explicit about where traces go.
- The quickstart sets the `WANDB_API_KEY` environment variable to your CoreWeave Forge API key before calling `weave.init` [S1].

## Get started with Weave

Weave provides SDKs for Python and TypeScript. Both SDKs support tracing, evaluation, datasets, and the core Weave features. Some advanced features, such as class-based Models and Scorers, aren't available in the Weave TypeScript SDK.

To get started with Weave:

1. Create a CoreWeave Forge account at [https://id.coreweave.com/signup](https://id.coreweave.com/signup) and get your API key from [https://forge.coreweave.com/settings#apikeys](https://forge.coreweave.com/settings#apikeys?utm_source=course\&utm_medium=course\&utm_campaign=weave).
2. Install Weave:

   ```python Python theme={"system"}
   pip install weave
   ```

   ```typescript TypeScript theme={"system"}
   npm install weave
   ```
3. In your script, import Weave and initialize a project. Replace `<your-team>` with your CoreWeave Forge team name and `<your-project>` with your Weights & Biases project name.

   ```python Python theme={"system"}
   import weave
   client = weave.init('<your-team>/<your-project>')
   ```

   ```typescript TypeScript theme={"system"}
   import * as weave from 'weave';
   const client = await weave.init('<your-team>/<your-project>');
   ```

You're now ready to use Weave.

# What is Weave?

> Learn about W&B Weave and how it helps you build, evaluate, and improve LLM applications

W\&B Weave is an observability and evaluation platform for building reliable agents and LLM applications. Weave helps you understand what your AI application is doing, measure how well it performs, and systematically improve it over time.

Building LLM applications is fundamentally different from traditional software development. LLM outputs are non-deterministic, making debugging harder. Quality is subjective and context-dependent. Small prompt changes can cause unexpected behavior changes. Traditional testing approaches fall short.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

## Getting started

To enable Weave tracing for your Verdict pipelines, call `weave.init(project=...)` at the beginning of your script. Use the `project` argument to log to a specific Weights & Biases Team name with `team-name/project-name`, or pass `project-name` to log to your default team or entity.

```python lines {7} theme={"system"}
import weave
from verdict import Pipeline
from verdict.common.judge import JudgeUnit
from verdict.schema import Schema

# Initialize Weave with your project name
weave.init("verdict_demo")

# Create a simple evaluation pipeline
pipeline = Pipeline()
pipeline = pipeline >> JudgeUnit().prompt("Rate the quality of this text: {source.text}")

# Create sample data
data = Schema.of(text="This is a sample text for evaluation.")

# Run the pipeline - Weave traces this automatically
output = pipeline.run(data)

print(output)
```

# Verdict

> Use Verdict evaluation framework with Weave to trace and monitor your LLM evaluation pipelines

[GitHub source](https://github.com/wandb/examples/blob/master/weave/docs/quickstart_verdict.ipynb)

Weave is designed to track and log all calls made through the [Verdict Python library](https://verdict.haizelabs.com/docs/) automatically.

When working with AI evaluation pipelines, debugging matters. Whether a pipeline step fails, outputs are unexpected, or nested operations create confusion, pinpointing issues can be hard. Verdict applications often consist of multiple pipeline steps, judges, and transformations, so it helps to understand the inner workings of your evaluation workflows.

Weave streamlines this process by automatically capturing traces for your [Verdict](https://verdict.readthedocs.io/) applications. This lets you monitor and analyze your pipeline's performance to debug and optimize your AI evaluation workflows.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

- The quickstart sets the `WANDB_API_KEY` environment variable to your CoreWeave Forge API key before calling `weave.init` [S1].
